mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening in monetary policy and inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are above their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both above 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS are above their 6-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the civilian unemployment rate to or below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) continues to rise signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage inflation and cost pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE ≤ 4% and PAYEMS rising for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE ≤ 4% and PAYEMS is rising for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces construction-related economic activity and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST is below its 12-month MA for six consecutive months.
